title: Retorsion: tradition's integrity faces the same demand — Bellarmine's 'no new revelations' collapses
source_text: XXXVI. Sed illi possunt simili difficultate urgeri. Dicam enim eodem modo, Non tantum necesse est, ut sciamus Apostolos doctrinam a Christo acceptam Ecclesiae Pastoribus & Rectoribus sine scripto magna ex parte tradidisse, & simpliciter fidei illorum commisisse, sed etiam ut certi simus traditiones illas Apostolicas per tot saecula ad nos pervenisse integras atque incorruptas. Istud autem non possumus ex ipsa Apostolica traditione discere. Igitur necesse est ut praeter verbum illud quod Apostoli partim scripto, partim viva voce tradiderunt, in Ecclesia extet aliud Dei verbum, per quod hodierna Ecclesia certa reddatur tam Scripturas quam traditiones integras & incorruptas ad ipsam pervenisse. Adeoque falsum est, quod Bellarminus cum Pontificiorum doctissimis quibusque & probatissimis asserit, Ecclesiam nunc non regi novis revelationibus, sed in iis permanere quae tradiderunt illi qui ministri fuerunt sermonis: Et illa omnia quae Ecclesia fide tenet, tradita fuisse ab Apostolis, aut Prophetis, aut scripto, aut verbo. De verbo Dei non scripto lib. 4. cap. 9. Quod si quis dicat fideles certos reddi de sinceritate & integritate tum Scripturae, tum traditionum per testimonium Ecclesiae quae errare non potest, difficultatem hanc minime tollet. Nam quaeritur unde hoc discat Ecclesia ipsa, & quo fundamento nitatur hac in parte ipsius Ecclesiae fides.
pass_a_gloss: But they can be pressed with a similar difficulty. For I will say in the same way, It is necessary not only that we know that the Apostles delivered the doctrine received from Christ to the Pastors and Rulers of the Church without writing for a great part, and simply committed it to their faith, but also that we be certain that those Apostolic traditions have come down to us through so many ages integral and uncorrupted. But that we cannot learn from the Apostolic tradition itself. Therefore it is necessary that besides that word which the Apostles delivered partly by writing, partly by living voice, there exist in the Church another word of God, by which today's Church may be made certain that both the Scriptures and the traditions have come to it integral and uncorrupted. And so that is false which Bellarmine with the most learned and approved of the Pontificians asserts, that the Church is not now ruled by new revelations, but remains in those things which those delivered who were ministers of the word: And that all those things which the Church holds by faith were delivered by the Apostles, or Prophets, either by writing or by word. On the unwritten word of God, book 4, chapter 9. Which if anyone should say that the faithful are made certain of the sincerity and integrity both of Scripture and of traditions by the testimony of the Church which cannot err, he will by no means remove this difficulty. For it is asked whence the Church itself learns this, and on what foundation the faith of the Church itself rests in this part.
pass_b_english: Same demand hits oral tradition: we must know Apostolic deliveries reached us intact across ages — yet tradition cannot certify its own integrity.
So Rome would need yet another divine word beyond Scripture-plus-tradition to guarantee both arrived uncorrupted.
That falsifies Bellarmine's claim that the Church needs no new revelations and only keeps what Apostles and Prophets delivered.
Appealing to an infallible Church's testimony does not help — whence does the Church itself learn, and on what does its faith rest?
